avoid_for: Consumer retail, playful multi-color brands, loud startup launches, or any context needing bold or emotional typography — the whisper-weight PolySans, 95% achromatic restraint, asymmetric cut-corner cards, and generous whitespace are a quiet editorial voice that reads like a printed annual report, not a hype page.
best_for: Data-product and analytics SaaS landing pages (observability, finance dashboards, B2B data platforms) that want an editorial observatory feel — warm paper-white canvas, monospaced-precision data cards, a single orange ember as highlight, weight-400 PolySans headlines, and chart widgets as the imagery.
name: Ventriloc
palette_voice: A warm paper-white canvas (#ffffff) with warm-gray surfaces (Ash #efefef, Fog #f5f5f5, Ivory #ebe6dd) — warm grays and ivory instead of cool tech-blue; Graphite (#202020) anchors all text and the dark filled CTA; a single Ember Orange (#ff682c) punctuates the monochrome like a highlighter on a printed report — used only for link underlines, chart highlights, and small icon accents, never as a CTA fill; Brass (#816729) adds a muted warm counterpoint for chart strokes and tags. Pages stay 95% achromatic.
signature_moves: The asymmetric border-radius 6px 0px 0px on featured cards — a single cut corner that signals editorial layout instead of a standard card grid, paired with 0px-radius buttons and 200px-radius nav pills (a three-radius system: sharp → asymmetric → fully round)
PolySans at weight 400 with -0.02em tracking for every heading, nav item, and button label — whisper-weight editorial authority that no bold headline could replicate
The 66px display headline at line-height 0.91 with -1.32px tracking — a tight, poster-like typographic statement on white canvas
Dark Graphite-filled sharp-cornered CTA button (0px radius) contrasted against the soft rounded card system

Data dashboard cards (line charts, stat rings, revenue widgets) in Ember Orange and Brass strokes floating on warm-gray surfaces — the charts ARE the imagery, no shadows, alternating white/ash bands instead of dividers

source.leading_note: fallback, no --leading-body token in variables.css (scale only has caption/subheading/heading/display); DESIGN.md describes 16px PolySans/1.0 for buttons and body in Inter 1.15–1.50; tokens.json base body step is Inter 15px at 1.33
source.radius: asymmetric-card 6px 0px 0px, cards 8px, data-widgets 20px, buttons 0px, nav-pills 200px, tags 20px
source.shadow: none — depth comes from surface-color contrast (white/ash alternation), no box-shadows on cards or buttons

tagline: Editorial data observatory on warm paper — a single orange ember punctuating monochrome precision.
typographic_voice: A two-face system where PolySans (subst. Inter Tight/Space Grotesk) is the voice and Inter is the grammar: PolySans at weight 400 only (never 500/600) with -0.02em tracking across headings, nav items, and button labels, with the 66px display at 0.91 leading; Inter handles all body copy, captions, and metadata at 400–600; line-height never exceeds 1.25 on display headings; the tight letter-spacing compensates for the light weight at large sizes, keeping headlines precise and architectural.
